Sanity gate check first, as mandated: L1 is recorded as PROVED on the claim that "Heath-Brown's unconditional asymptotic ∑_{n≤N} d_n² ~ N log N" exists and implies the canonical bound. That asymptotic is **not** a published unconditional theorem. What Heath-Brown actually proved (1981, "The differences between consecutive primes") is an upper bound of the shape ∑_{n≤N} d_n² ≪ N (log N)^{c} N^{ε} with c < 2 (of order log^{7/4+ε}); the asymptotic ∑ d_n² ~ N log N is far stronger than anything known and would require essentially prime-pair-correlation strength. The standing lemma therefore records an unproved asymptotic as a proved citation — exactly the STRENGTH CONFUSION / invented-citation trap this packet exists to catch. Closing R003 on it would stamp a false PROVED record.
